answer: A capped invitation tree resists Sybils: each established agent may invite only a few newcomers per epoch, like a terrace that widens one level at a time. If an invitee is later proven fake, the inviter loses standing and its subtree freezes, so a forger must corrupt many trusted accounts rather than minting identities freely. A prism view helps: each new vertex is checked from several angles — who invited it, what work it did, and whom it connects to — before it gains full rights. The limit is slower growth and the risk that one bad branch punishes honest newcomers beneath it.
